question: Who among the following kings founded a suburban township near Vijayanagara called Nagalapuram?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishnadevaraya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Krishnadevaraya:**

 
 
• Krishnadevaraya, the ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire, founded the suburban township of **Nagalapuram** near Vijayanagara.
 
• He named the town after his mother, Nagala Devi, as a tribute to her.
 
• Krishnadevaraya was one of the greatest rulers of the Vijayanagara Empire, reigning from 1509 to 1529.
 
• He was a patron of art, literature, and architecture, and his reign is considered the golden age of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• Nagalapuram was developed as a cultural and administrative center during his rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deva Raya II:**

 
 
• Deva Raya II was a prominent ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire who reigned from 1424 to 1446.
 
• He is known for his military conquests and administrative reforms.
 
• However, he is not associated with the founding of Nagalapuram.
 
• His reign is marked by the expansion of the empire and patronage of literature and arts.
 
• He is often referred to as one of the most powerful rulers of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
 
 
• **Rajaraja Chola:**
 
 
• Rajaraja Chola I was a great Chola emperor who ruled from 985 to 1014 CE.
 
• He is renowned for his military conquests, architectural achievements, and the construction of the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur.
 
• His reign marked the peak of the Chola Empire's power and influence.
 
• However, he belonged to the Chola dynasty and is not connected to the Vijayanagara Empire or Nagalapuram.
 
• His contributions were primarily in South India, particularly in Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• **Rajendra I:**
 
 
• Rajendra Chola I, the son of Rajaraja Chola, ruled from 1014 to 1044 CE.
 
• He expanded the Chola Empire to its greatest extent, including parts of Southeast Asia.
 
• He is known for his naval expeditions and the construction of the city of Gangaikonda Cholapuram.
 
• Like Rajaraja Chola, he belonged to the Chola dynasty and is unrelated to the Vijayanagara Empire or Nagalapuram.
 
• His reign is celebrated for its military and cultural achievements.
